hook.text: A compound from a deep-sea sponge became a cancer drug—the ocean may hold thousands more.

buildup.text: Marine organisms produce unique chemicals for defense and survival—many have pharmaceutical potential.

discovery.text: Enzymes from vent bacteria work at extreme heat—useful for industrial processes and DNA amplification (PCR).

twist.text: Only 5% of deep-sea species have been studied for useful compounds—the potential is barely scratched.

climax.text: Access and benefit-sharing rules are still being debated—who owns the chemistry of the deep sea?

punchline.text: The next wonder drug may sit on the bottom of the ocean.

quiz.question: What is bioprospecting?
options: Searching marine organisms for useful compounds
